title: "Deployment and Rollback"
execute:
  eval: false

Production provisioning is an administrator handoff. Repository delivery does
not authorize the agent or developer to provision the VM, request certificates,
create mail identities, or declare the external gates complete.

## Host and package preflight

The checked production target is Ubuntu 26.04 on `amd64`. Before installing,
compare the selected package and OS against the current [Posit platform support
matrix](https://docs.posit.co/platform-support.html) and [Shiny Server
guidance](https://docs.posit.co/shiny-server/). A script override is acceptable
only for a named test host with a written exception; it is not a production
approval.

The repository review on 2026-09-26 found Ubuntu 26.04 LTS listed for Posit
server products, while the current Shiny Server guidance still limits Shiny
Server itself to `x86-64`. The pinned package and preflight therefore require
`amd64`. Recheck both sources at installation time rather than treating this
dated review as permanent approval.

The Shiny Server installer consumes a local `.deb` and a separately reviewed
SHA-256. It validates the package name, exact version, package architecture,
host architecture, and checksum before calling the package manager:

```bash
sudo scripts/install_shiny_server.sh \
  --env /root/ppsv-app.env \
  --deb /absolute/path/shiny-server-1.5.23.1030-amd64.deb
```

No repository script downloads an installer. R dependencies are pinned in
`ppsv-app/renv.lock`; its reviewed `renv.lock.sha256` must verify before a
restore or deployment proceeds.

## TLS inputs and validation

The operator must supply three distinct, absolute paths:

- `TLS_CERT_FILE`: leaf certificate for `ppcf-vm.biochem.mpg.de`;
- `TLS_BUNDLE_FILE`: leaf-first full chain; and
- `TLS_KEY_FILE`: the exact matching private key.

`TLS_KEY_FILE` is intentionally unresolved in the sample environment. Never
guess it, reuse a CSR path, or treat a certificate request as a key.

Before copying anything into `/etc/ssl`, provisioning validates:

1. all inputs are readable regular files;
2. the leaf is a PEM certificate;
3. the hostname is covered by the certificate SAN;
4. the leaf has at least 30 days remaining;
5. the private key is valid and usable unattended;
6. certificate and private-key public keys match;
7. the bundle starts with the same leaf; and
8. the presented intermediate chain verifies the leaf.

Only after those checks pass is the full chain installed as
`/etc/ssl/certs/ppsv-app-fullchain.pem` and the key as
`/etc/ssl/private/ppsv-app.key` with mode `0600`. Apache configuration must pass
`apache2ctl configtest` before reload. Acceptance uses normal CA validation;
`curl -k` is forbidden because it would hide a broken certificate or chain.

For renewal, obtain the new matching key/certificate/chain through the approved
PKI workflow, point a protected operator environment at those inputs, rerun
provisioning, and repeat the full TLS acceptance check. Do not overwrite the
active key manually.

## Idempotent provisioning

Create the operator environment from the tracked sample and fill all required
values. A temporary root-owned, mode-`0600` source is safe before the private
runtime group exists:

```bash
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0600 \
  scripts/ppsv-app.env.example /root/ppsv-app.env
sudoedit /root/ppsv-app.env
sudo scripts/provision.sh --env /root/ppsv-app.env --install-system
```

Provisioning installs the final environment at
`/etc/ppsv-app/ppsv-app.env`, root-owned with group `ppsvf-shiny` and mode
`0640`. It creates or validates:

- runtime user `ppsvf-shiny-user` and private primary group `ppsvf-shiny`;
- immutable-release, persistent-data, fallback, lock, deployment-record, and
  renv-cache directories;
- project-pool setgid/default ACL access for the service account and
  `b_profa`;
- the required external backup directories;
- loopback-only Shiny Server configuration;
- HTTP redirect and HTTPS LDAP/WebSocket Apache sites; and
- systemd units for the mail worker, backup, and pool reconciliation.

It refuses production values other than `AUTH_MODE=ldap`, the canonical public
URL, the private runtime identity, and `b_profa` as the pool ACL group.

## Apache and Shiny behavior

The installed Shiny configuration uses:

```text
run_as ppsvf-shiny-user;
listen 3838 127.0.0.1;
```

The port-80 site redirects every request to HTTPS. The HTTPS site redirects `/`
to `/ppsv-app/`, authenticates that location with LDAP, strips client identity
headers, injects the server-authenticated profile, and proxies ordinary HTTP
and WebSocket upgrades to loopback.

Do not expose 3838, place a second unauthenticated proxy in front of it, or
enable a test/local login on the production host.

## First deployment

Use a clean Git worktree at the reviewed revision. Production deployment stops
on tracked or untracked changes unless an explicit test-only dirty-release
override is set.

```bash
sudo scripts/deploy.sh --source "$PWD"
```

The release identifier defaults to a UTC timestamp plus commit. An operator may
supply a safe explicit ID:

```bash
sudo scripts/deploy.sh --source "$PWD" --release 20260925-approved
```

Deployment performs these stages:

1. copy only `ppsv-app/` into a new staging directory, excluding secrets,
   databases, fallback uploads, and stale package libraries;
2. bootstrap the single pinned `renv` package through its checked autoloader
   when absent, then restore exactly `ppsv-app/renv.lock` into the staged
   application;
3. run requirements and Java mail-runtime checks;
4. create and verify a pre-deployment SQLite/fallback backup when persistent
   state already exists;
5. stop the mail worker and Shiny;
6. initialize a fresh PPSV database only if absent, or apply PPSV migrations
   transactionally;
7. write revision and SHA-256 manifest metadata;
8. make the staged release root-owned and immutable to the runtime user;
9. atomically change `/srv/shiny-server/ppsv-app`; and
10. start Shiny, require a successful loopback health check, restart timers,
    and run local verification.

`PPSV_RESET_DB=1` is rejected. The copied MS database is neither read nor
migrated.

## Verification

Run the complete local/public verifier after deployment. Full acceptance
requires a dedicated LDAP test netrc and an ordinary active LDAP username;
technician/admin checks default to `grzejszc` and `yeroslaviz` unless explicit
alternatives are supplied:

```bash
sudo scripts/verify_deployment.sh \
  --netrc /root/ppsv-test.netrc \
  --role-user ORDINARY_LDAP_USERNAME
```

It checks release placement and protected parent modes, absence of mutable
state in the release, the reviewed lock checksum, service
status, loopback binding, worker UID, database integrity and mode, storage
permissions and the recorded facility-pool mount source, Apache
modules/configuration/header stripping, timers, trusted TLS redirects, and
unauthenticated identity spoof rejection. Supply a temporary
mode-`0600` netrc to include an authenticated LDAP route test:

```bash
sudo scripts/verify_deployment.sh \
  --netrc /root/ppsv-test.netrc \
  --role-user ORDINARY_LDAP_USERNAME \
  --role-technician grzejszc \
  --role-admin yeroslaviz
```

The verifier also refuses readiness while the service-sender authorization,
ticket end-to-end test, or pool-snapshot-policy acknowledgement remains `0`,
and verifies that the external backup mount has the recorded source. It
supplements rather than replaces the manual browser, ticket, role, and restore
tests in [Acceptance and handoff](acceptance.qmd).

## Code rollback

List immutable releases and select an existing reviewed target:

```bash
sudo find /srv/ppsv-app/releases -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -printf '%f\n'
sudo scripts/rollback.sh --release RELEASE_ID
```

Rollback atomically changes the code symlink, restarts Shiny, and requires a
successful loopback health check. If that check fails, it restores the previous
code link.

Code rollback does **not** reverse database migrations or remove requests
created since the release. The deployment health-failure path also keeps any
already committed migration. Restore a database only after assessing schema
compatibility and explicitly accepting loss of newer state.

## Configuration changes

Edit `/etc/ppsv-app/ppsv-app.env` with `sudoedit`, preserve root ownership and
mode `0640` or stricter, and run the relevant validation before restarting
services. For TLS, identity, path, user, or Apache changes, rerun provisioning
rather than applying ad hoc edits. For mail-mode changes, complete the decision
test in [Mail and storage operations](mail-storage.qmd) and retain its evidence.
